prompt: The α-hydrogen of a ketone has pKa ~20. Why is it so much more acidic than a comparable sp³ C–H (pKa ~50)?

options.label: The resulting enolate is resonance-stabilized by the adjacent C=O.

explanation: Deprotonation gives an enolate; the negative charge delocalizes onto the carbonyl oxygen via resonance, which is a huge stabilizing effect.
